breath literacy: the skill school skipped. You learned to read. Now learn to breathe.

Begin with Breath is your foundation course in breath literacy. Becoming aware of your breath is the first step in reclaiming your nervous system health. In 6 live classes, you will learn more than 30 breathing practices, when to use each one, and how they affect your nervous system so that you can calm your mind, sleep better, and find energy on demand.

Taught by Esther Kalaba, Registered Psychotherapist: “After 20 years in mental health, I believe this is the most important skill you can learn.”

Save your spot See the six weeks

$295 CAD. Live on Zoom four times a year, and every class is recorded.

“I know I should breathe. I just don’t know how.”

Of course you don’t. You learned to read, write and do long division, but nobody ever taught you the one thing you do all day, every day. So most of us breathe short and shallow, high in the chest, and call it stress.

After 20 years working in mental health, I believe breathing well is the most important skill you can learn. Almost everyone who comes to me with anxiety, burnout or depression is barely breathing, and few people know what short and shallow breath does to their mental health and wellbeing. Breathing well is one of the simplest and cheapest ways to change your emotional and mental state quickly and support how you feel.

Begin with Breath grew out of the free online breathing classes I offered during the pandemic. The group that kept coming back became the People of the Prana.

Calm isn’t something you’re born with. It’s something you practice. (And it’s much easier than you think.)

Breathing well isn’t just about chilling out, though it does that beautifully. When you learn to slow your breath down and work with it on purpose, you get your choice back: over what you focus on, how you respond and how you feel in your body. With regular practice it can bring more energy and focus, better sleep and a steadier mood, and over time stress stops knocking you over so easily.

And honestly? Breathing well just feels good. It brings clarity, calm and (surprise!) really great people into your life.

Esther Kalaba, MA, RP

breath literacy.

It starts with noticing your breath.

Breath literacy is the process of becoming breath aware: the first step in reclaiming your nervous system. Breathing well has an alphabet, just like reading: your posture, the muscles you breathe with, the route your breath takes, the length of each inhale and exhale, and the pause in between. Once you know it, you can read your own state and change it, on purpose, in a few breaths.

  1. Step 1

    Learn the letters.

    The fundamentals of pranayama: posture, the diaphragm, nose or mouth, and where these practices come from.

  2. Step 2

    Learn the words.

    More than 30 practices from the Kundalini and Hatha yoga traditions and modern psychology, from long deep breathing to Breath of Fire.

  3. Step 3

    Learn when to use them.

    Which breath calms you, which wakes you up, and which helps you focus, sleep or let go, so you know what to reach for when stress shows up.

With consistent practice you build resilience to stress, so you can literally breathe your way through anything.

six weeks, six live classes.

Peek inside Begin with Breath.

Each week you learn 5 to 8 practices, the why behind them, and you get plenty of time to actually breathe. By the end you’ll know more than 30 practices and when to use each one. It’s like having a medicine chest (no pun intended) right in your own body.

  1. Week 18 practices

    Long & Deep Breathingor, why breathe now?

    • Get to know your natural breath and how it shapes your mental and emotional state.
    • The fundamentals of pranayama: posture, muscle use and technique, and its rich history.
    • Breath awareness, long deep breathing and your own breath signature.
  2. Week 27 practices

    The Three Diaphragmssensing from the inside

    • Interoception: the inner art of sensing and knowing what your body is telling you.
    • The three diaphragms behind your breath and voice, and the yogic locks (bandhas).
    • Nose or mouth? How your breathing route affects your nervous system.
  3. Week 38 practices

    The Energetics of Breathingyour powerhouse

    • Your navel point and diaphragm, and Breath of Fire with its energizing effect.
    • Prana, the life force energy, and how it moves through you.
    • The vayus, the nadis, your electromagnetic field, and the link between breath and creativity.
  4. Week 45 practices

    Focus on the Inhaleunderstanding inspiration

    • What is awareness? What is consciousness? Let’s explore.
    • Feel your feelings through the inhale, and receive the breath with trust and presence.
    • Breath suspensions on the inhale, and segmented breathing.
  5. Week 55 practices

    Focus on the Exhaleletting go

    • Meet apana, the downward flowing force that supports release.
    • Breath suspensions on the exhale, for grounding and clearing.
    • Shunniya, the meditative state of deep silence, and the breath as a healing tool.
  6. Week 6Your toolkit

    Your Breath Is Your Medicineintegration

    • Revisit the highlights of the past five weeks.
    • How the breath helps you love yourself and others more fully.
    • Build your breath medicine chest: a custom toolkit for everyday life.

By week six, you’ll know:

  • How to actually breathe, not just think about doing it.
  • The essential techniques: long deep breathing, segmented breath, Breath of Fire, breath suspensions, alternate nostril breathing and more.
  • The science behind why breathing works.
  • How your breath shapes your thoughts, emotions, body and stress levels, and which tools to rely on when things get stressful.
  • How to listen to your body, including muscles you never knew you had.
  • How not to take it all so seriously. (Yes, laughter is in the curriculum. Joy is part of the medicine.)

a word from Esther.

“Your breath is a gift.”

I have been teaching these practices for over 20 years now, in the context of my clinical practice, with kids as young as five and people well into their eighties. What I come back to again and again is how utterly fundamental breath is to every part of our lives: physical, mental, emotional and spiritual.

Learning to breathe is not a luxury. It is a necessity, especially in these stressful times on the planet. My mission is to make conscious breathing available to as many people as possible, so that it is taught regularly in schools, workplaces, hospitals and beyond.

I am so honoured and excited to share these healing practices with you.

with gratitude and love,Esther Kalaba, MA, RPCo-founder, People of the Prana

Questions people ask before they begin with breath.

How does Begin with Breath fit with BEAT + BREATH™?

BEAT + BREATH™ is the easy daily habit: three minute tracks set to a beat that slow your breath down. Begin with Breath is the foundation underneath it: more than 30 practices, why they work and when to use each one, for anyone who wants to understand their breath and go deeper. You can start with either, and many people keep their daily BEAT + BREATH™ practice going while they take the course.

Do I need any experience with yoga or breathwork?

Nope. Begin with Breath is perfect for total beginners and just as valuable for experienced breathers who want to deepen their practice. Everything is explained step by step, each class is adjusted to the people in the room, and there’s plenty of time for your questions. Many people take the course more than once to take the practices even deeper. Learning to breathe is a lifelong practice.

What if I can’t attend the live classes?

No problem. Every class is recorded and uploaded, so you can watch (and re‑breathe) on your own time. Many people take the whole course on replay and still get the full benefit.

What kind of approach do you use?

The course brings together practices from Kundalini yoga, Hatha yoga and Sat Nam Rasayan with principles from somatic therapy, trauma informed practice and Western psychology. It’s a down to earth, practical approach to the science and experience of breathing well, designed to fit into daily life. You learn by doing, because that’s how this material really sinks in.

What does a typical class look like?

Each week you learn 5 to 8 breathing practices and some of the theory behind them, and you practice them together. By the end of the six weeks you’ll have learned more than 30 practices and know when to use each one.

How is this different from breathwork videos on YouTube?

This isn’t follow-along breathing. It’s a structured course where each week builds on the last, so you learn how breath affects your nervous system, your emotions and your mind, and how to use it in real life. You also get direct feedback, time for your questions and a supportive community. As Esther likes to say, “So many issues can be bypassed through simply changing your breathing pattern.”

What if I have anxiety, trauma or a mental health diagnosis?

Begin with Breath was designed with mental health in mind and is taught by a Registered Psychotherapist. It’s breath education, not therapy, and many people take it alongside therapy or as part of their healing. If you have specific concerns, email us at breathe@peopleoftheprana.com. For a course focused on your nervous system and trauma, see the Nervous System First Aid Kit.

Can I take this as a wellness professional or yoga teacher?

Yes! It’s a great foundation for yoga teachers, therapists, social workers, coaches, educators and health care professionals. Take it as Begin with Breath for Professionals and you’ll join a few additional classes and write a short exam to earn CE credits, so you can confidently offer these practices to your clients. See the professional track.

Is it weird that I don’t know how to breathe properly?

Not at all. Most people breathe in a way that’s shallow, rushed or dysregulated, especially when they’re stressed. That’s exactly why this course exists. You’re not behind. You’re right on time.

Is breathing safe?

The practices in this course are safe and suitable for almost everyone. Please let us know at the start if you have a condition such as high blood pressure, or if you’re pregnant, as there are certain practices we’ll ask you not to do. We also ask that you never practice in water, while driving, or while operating tools or machinery.

Will there be homework?

We recommend 5 to 10 minutes of practice a day, so you can experience the teachings for yourself. Each week we’ll guide you with a short routine to help it stick: like brushing your teeth, but think of it as hygiene for your nervous system. You’ll also have the manual, the course notes, the recorded meditations, and two months of Wake Up & Breathe mornings for free.

How is the course offered?

Live online on Zoom four times a year, and in person twice a year as The Art of Breath, a four day retreat at the SEED Lodge. The next retreat is January 7 to 10, 2027. The next online round runs on Monday evenings, January 11 to February 15, 2027, at 8 p.m. Eastern. Save your spot. start with the free app and breathe with us.
